themes_detail.label: Park Noise Crisis Explodes
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 4 this week compared to a 0.1 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 3100% surge (z-score: 11.72)—suggesting a new or dramatically worsening disturbance pattern in Fort Greene or Brooklyn Heights parks this week.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 11.72 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
reporting_angles: Visit the district's parks (Fort Greene Park, Brooklyn Bridge Park edges) to observe and document the noise source—live music, events, construction, gatherings?
Interview Parks Department about permits issued or events scheduled in the past 2 weeks
Talk to residents near parks about timing, duration, and impact on quality of life

themes_detail.label: Broken Windows & Doors Spike
themes_detail.summary: Door and window damage complaints jumped 129% last week to 16 complaints compared to a 7.0 weekly average (z-score: 7.35), suggesting either a break-in wave or coordinated property damage in the district.
evidence: 16 door/window complaints last week vs. 7.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 7.35 indicates high statistical significance
129% increase from baseline suggests concentrated incident or pattern
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaints with NYPD crime data to determine if break-ins or vandalism is driving the spike
Map the 16 complaints geographically—are they clustered on specific blocks or spread across the district?
Interview precinct community affairs officer about any organized retail theft, burglary rings, or vandalism crews active this week

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Failures Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street light complaints surged 156% last week to 24 complaints compared to a 9.4 weekly average (z-score: 4.95), indicating potential widespread outages or failures in the district's street lighting infrastructure.
evidence: 24 street light complaints last week vs. 9.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.95 indicates statistically significant anomaly
156% increase suggests either equipment failure wave or concentrated outage zone
reporting_angles: Request DEP/ConEd data on outages, maintenance work, or equipment failures in the district last week
Canvass the district after dark to visually identify dark blocks and map them against complaint data
Interview DEP about response times and whether maintenance backlog or contractor issues explain the spike

themes_detail.label: Panhandling & Disorder Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints surged 327% last week to 8 complaints from a 1.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.49), and drug activity complaints peaked 2 weeks ago at 4 (433% above baseline)—signaling potential street disorder or loitering escalation.
evidence: 8 panhandling complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average; 327% increase
4 drug activity complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 baseline; 433% increase (z-score: 4.91)
Two separate disorder signals in consecutive weeks suggest emerging pattern
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD precinct about enforcement changes, withdrawn resources, or new hotspots in the past 2 weeks
Visit high-complaint blocks (use 311 address data) to assess visible disorder and talk to merchants/residents
Investigate whether recent shelter placements, transit hub activity, or seasonal factors explain the uptick

themes_detail.label: Tree & Vegetation Overgrowth
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints spiked 273% last week to 7 complaints compared to a 1.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.4), indicating either deferred Parks maintenance or seasonal growth season concerns.
evidence: 7 overgrown tree complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average
273% increase from baseline suggests localized maintenance gap or seasonal surge
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to determine if there is a maintenance backlog or contracted crew delay
Map the 7 complaints to identify if overgrowth is concentrated near schools, senior facilities, or high-traffic areas
Assess whether complaints correlate with spring/early summer growth season or reflect deferred winter work
